title: Phone features complement self-reports for questionnaire-defined risk labels
summary: In selected Korean smartphone participants, random-forest models combining passive features with daily self-reports achieved cross-validated ROC areas of0.82 for depression-risk labels and0.86 for anxiety-risk labels. These are weekly questionnaire-defined states, with overlapping symptom-report windows, not clinical diagnoses or future-onset forecasts.
organization: Electronics and Telecommunications Research Institute; Korea University; Batoners

source_review.scope: Actual original relevant clinical/computational Methods, reference labels, evaluation Results and limitations read

evidence.ai_role: Fitted tree ensembles combine mobility/activity summaries and brief symptom reports to classify weekly PHQ-9/GAD-7 threshold labels.
evidence.tested: Of455 recruited adults,277 depression and275 anxiety participants met coverage requirements. Repeated observations remained with their participant in fivefold evaluation; fourteen-day observation windows preceded weekly questionnaire dates.
evidence.unknown: Coverage thresholds and window length were selected using the same cross-validation framework, without an established untouched configuration test. Active daily mood/anxiety reports overlap conceptually and temporally with questionnaire references; weekly PHQ-9 repeats a two-week recall window. Many participants were excluded for coverage, and there was no external or temporal validation. Sleep features are phone-motion proxies. Average-precision numbers are not used here without independently resolving positive-class prevalence/encoding details. Prospective collection does not establish a prospectively frozen model or benefit.
